teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: Lose by 26 with the lowest score in the league and keep first place: the McButt Nuggets are living a life the rest of you can only dream about. Jordan grabbed Marcus Mariota this week, started him over Bo Nix, and got 5.3 from a quarterback who lasted eleven plays in London, while Nix scored 13.4 on the bench. Carnell Tate's 17 sat behind Garrett Wilson's 4.2, Rhamondre Stevenson's 16.9 sat behind Jeremiyah Love's 6, and the whole bench would have won the game by double digits. Jonathan Taylor did his part with 22, and rest-of-season projections keep the Nuggets afloat, but the committee is starting to wonder whether first place is a ranking or a lease. Jordan also scooped up De'Von Achane off Brett A.'s scrap heap and parked him on IR next to Jordyn Tyson, so the medical wing is well stocked. The running backs behind Taylor and Love are deep enough to sell; Stevenson is a real chip for a contender that needs a back.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: Four weeks in, Baker finally made a roster move, and the league should probably check on him. He added MarShawn Lloyd, Frum's castoff, and then did the even more shocking thing: he set a nearly perfect lineup, leaving under 4 points on the bench after leaving a small nation's worth there in the first three weeks. Chuba Hubbard went for 25, the Seahawks defense led the league with 12, and Cam Little kicked in 14, which was enough to beat Mike D. by about nine and climb three spots. Jahmyr Gibbs, the $71 keeper, was merely fine. The worry is the infirmary: Justin Jefferson, Rico Dowdle and Dallas Goedert are all out, and the only back behind Gibbs and Hubbard is Lloyd, who projects under 2 points a game. One hamstring and the Dino Nuggets are extinct, so Baker's second roster move of the season had better not take another four weeks.

teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: Dakota Johnson opened the top movie in America and hosted SNL in the same weekend, which is still less juggling than Mike D. trying to manage four quarterbacks on one roster. He picked up C.J. Stroud and started him for a strong 23, with Dak Prescott scoring 18 on the bench, Sam Darnold 13 on the bench, and Jayden Daniels on IR, a quarterback room with more depth than most NFL teams. The problem was everywhere else on the bench. Alvin Kamara scored 20.3 behind Cam Skattebo's 7.1, the swap that flipped a nine-point loss to Baker, and the Bills defense he picked up scored 1 on the day Drake Maye ran through Buffalo, while the Texans scored 3 on his bench. At least Javonte Williams, a $10 keeper, scored three touchdowns in the Cowboys-Texans shootout. The Cartel is still third on talent, with Skattebo and Kamara as spare backs and a quarterback for every day of the week.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: Foy once called his team LuckDynasty and The Flip Phones, and the dynasty is back in business. He won with the seventh-best score of the week because he drew Jordan on the one Sunday Jordan forgot how football works, and that's how you climb three spots without breaking a sweat. Kyren Williams carried the load with nearly 32, more than double his projection. The defense shuffle continues to be a hobby rather than a strategy: Foy cut the Giants after they scored 9 for him on the bench, picked up the Chiefs defense Sam had just dropped, started them, and got 1, while the Eagles scored 2 on his bench. Romeo Doubs scored 20.8 on the bench too, behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 6 in the flex, which would have been a crisis in a closer game. With Ladd McConkey questionable and six receivers on the roster, Foy has wide receivers to deal, and with the second-hardest remaining schedule in the league, he should cash in the luck while it's still worth something.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: Sam finally started the right defense, the Vikings for 10 on a day Minnesota won without scoring a touchdown, and it was the only thing that went right. Mark hung 150 on him, the Dootron dropped three spots, and the receiver he kept for $10, Parker Washington, scored 1.5 while Devaughn Vele scored 14.4 on the bench. Sam did make a good move: he grabbed Michael Wilson, flagged on draft day as Frum's best value, started him and got 13. He also cut Jaxson Dart, a $10 keeper, which is less a roster move than an admission. Bijan went for 27 and remains the whole act, and with Jordan Mason on IR, the only back behind Bijan and Omarion Hampton projects for basically nothing. Sam has four startable receivers and one starting running back too few, and the trade writes itself.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: Hearn has scored more points than anyone in the league and owns the best all-play record, and he is 2-2 and sixth, which is the fantasy equivalent of a great restaurant with a one-star Yelp page. Danny's 126 beat him this week, and Josh Downs' 3.1 in the flex while Malik Washington scored 9.5 on the bench didn't help. The defense, at least, is fixed: Hearn dropped the Jaguars and stuck with the Packers, who scored 10, the third-best number in the league, while Jacksonville scored 4 on Jordan's bench. Then he picked up Keenan Allen, who is out, which is a bold way to add depth. With Caleb Williams out, Purdy is the only quarterback left, and with A.J. Brown and Alec Pierce on IR, Deebo Samuel is the receiver depth, at about 6 a game. Pierce, a $10 keeper, has produced under a point per dollar, the worst return of any keeper in the league.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: The Ammonia Coladas scored 150.5, beat all eleven teams in the all-play, and won by 53, and the most remarkable part is that it could have been 177. Drake Maye torched the Bills for 26 on Mark's bench, Brian Robinson Jr. scored 25.2 behind Bucky Irving's 6.1, and the committee is honestly unsure whether to applaud or call for an audit. Nico Collins came back from IR and went for 27, Kyle Monangai played through a questionable tag for 27.5 on a projection under 8, and Sam LaPorta doubled his. Mark also picked up Keaton Mitchell from Mike D. and left him on the bench to score 8.8, because why stop now. The roster has eight running backs and none of them project like a real backup, but Mike Evans and Tee Higgins give Mark spare receivers to sell, and a team that just went 11-0 in the all-play has every reason to buy.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: The Tacos lost by nearly 30 to a team that hadn't won all season, and the culprit was the same $51 problem as always. Saquon Barkley played through a questionable tag for 1.5 points, giving him 21 for the season, while RJ Harvey scored 14.3 on the bench, and Travis Kelce posted 2.5 while Kyle Pitts outscored him from the bench. Saquon was flagged as Brett's worst pick on draft day, and that prediction is aging like milk in a hot car. Brett cleaned house this week, dropping De'Von Achane to Jordan's IR and Jordan Love to waivers, and the pickup who did play, Mack Hollins, scored 6.8 in the lineup. With DeVonta Smith out, the receiver behind Chris Olave and Michael Pittman Jr. is Makai Lemon, at about 5 a game, so the real hole on this roster is at wide receiver, and the running back room has enough bodies to fix it.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Danny finally won, and naturally he did it the Danny way: second-best score of the week, a 10-1 all-play, and nearly 38 points on the bench, the most in the league. Verity, a thriller about a ghostwriter, topped the box office this weekend, and Danny's bench has been ghostwriting his best games all season. This week's chapter: Emanuel Wilson, picked up after Frum cut him, scored 25.5 on the bench behind Matthew Golden's 10, Tucker Kraft scored 13.5 behind Dalton Kincaid's 1.2, and Rome Odunze outscored DJ Moore by 10. CeeDee Lamb's 17-catch day in the Cowboys-Texans shootout covered for all of it. The running back room is still a ward, with Travis Etienne and Isiah Pacheco on IR and Rachaad White out, which makes Wilson the backup by default. Danny is 1-3 with the worst luck number in the league; the curse is real, but the lineup card is helping it.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: A manager who once named his team Brockin' Big Tetas finally got Brock and Teta to show up on the same Sunday. Tetairoa McMillan went for 38.2 out of the flex on a career night with Bryce Young, Brock Bowers added 17.6, and Jeff even started Patrick Mahomes over Jalen Hurts, the right call for the first time all season. The result was the third-best score of the week, a nearly 30-point win over the reigning champ and a first win at last. The lineup still had its moments: Rashee Rice started through a questionable tag and scored zero while Khalil Shakir scored 9.7 on the bench, and Tony Pollard outscored Braelon Allen from the bench as well. With Breece Hall and Tank Bigsby both out, the backs behind Quinshon Judkins and Pollard project under 5 a game, so Jeff should turn one of his spare receivers into a running back. He has the softest remaining schedule in the league, and for once, the Amigos have a reason to drop the question mark.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Matthew Stafford led a fourth-quarter comeback in Philadelphia on Sunday, which would be great news if Hess's lineup had a fourth quarter. Stafford gave him 9.6, Puka Nacua's 23 did most of the lifting, and the Heavenly Woman scored 76.6, the second-lowest total of the week, and dropped three spots to eleventh. Hess finally started Kenyon Sadiq, a week after Sadiq scored 20 on his bench, and got a zero while Mark Andrews scored 11 on the bench, so the tight end timing is perfect in the worst possible way. The Kendre Miller pickup started in the flex and contributed 0.9. Hess has the fewest points in the league by more than 40, Jalen Coker is out, Jayden Reed and Jonathon Brooks are on IR, and the backups at running back and receiver both project around 4 a game. He needs help at two positions and has nothing anyone wants, so the trade market is going to involve a lot of pleading.

teams.name: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies

nameHistory.name: Lots of ??? But Tons of Upside!
Poopy Wake Up Call On Line Toot
The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Frum won by 35, posted a respectable 111.8, and is still last, which is a cruel thing to do to a team that beat seven others in the all-play. Young scored 21, Kenneth Walker went for 30 and Zay Flowers for 22, so the stars did their jobs. Then there's the lineup card. Ollie Gordon II, picked up this week, scored 17 on the bench while Dontayvion Wicks scored 3.3 in the flex; Colston Loveland outscored Dalton Schultz from the bench too; and Emanuel Wilson, cut by Frum, scored 25.5 for Danny. Frum once named his team DAMN IT DAVID!, and it remains the most accurate scouting report in the league. The Kansas City locker room reportedly wants Tyreek Hill back, and so does Frum, who is holding a roster spot for a receiver without a team. Behind Flowers and Jaylen Waddle there's Wicks at under 5 a game, so Frum should be shopping, and with the hardest remaining schedule in the league, quickly.

commentary.intro: Marcus Mariota got a start in London this weekend and lasted eleven plays, and somehow he still wasn't the strangest story in Fadunkadunk. That honor belongs to Jordan, who picked Mariota up, started him, posted the lowest score in the league, lost to all eleven teams in the all-play and kept first place anyway. The committee checked twice. Behind him, the board is a four-way pileup at 3-1, with Baker, Foy and Sam also at 3-1 and right on his heels, and Baker climbing three spots on the strength of a lineup he apparently set while awake. Mark put up the best score of the week by a mile and still left a starting running back's worth of points on his bench. And for the first time this season nobody is winless: Danny and Jeff both got off the schneid, which means the bottom of the standings is now a four-team support group at 1-3.

awards.lowScore: Jordan scored 75.4, lost to every team in the league in the all-play, and had nearly 38 points sitting on his bench, which would have beaten Foy with room to spare. The first-place team, everybody.
awards.toughestLoss: Mike D. lost by 8.9 with Alvin Kamara's 20.3 on the bench behind Cam Skattebo's 7.1, the only bench decision in the league this week that flipped a result.
awards.boom: Tetairoa McMillan was projected for 13.5 and scored 38.2 out of Jeff's flex, the biggest overperformance of the week and the first time in a month Jeff's lineup card looked like a plan.
awards.highScore: Mark, 150.5, a perfect 11-0 in the all-play, with Drake Maye and Brian Robinson Jr. combining for 51 on the bench.
awards.blowout: Mark over Sam by 53.4. Sam brought a lineup; Mark brought a lineup and a bench that also would have won.
awards.luckiestWin: Foy won with the seventh-best score of the week, because he drew the one team that scored the fewest.
awards.benchBomb: Mark benched Brian Robinson Jr. (25.2) for Bucky Irving (6.1), a 19-point swing that cost him nothing but a cleaner box score.
awards.worstDefense: Mike D.'s Bills, a fresh pickup, scored 1 on the day Drake Maye ran them over, the worst defensive score in the league.
awards.bestDefense: Baker's Seahawks led all defenses with 12, and for once Baker had the good one in his lineup.

commentary.outro:
Week 5 is loaded at the top. Jordan gets Sam in a battle of 3-1 teams that both had a Sunday to forget, and Baker gets Foy in another 3-1 matchup, the cleanest lineup in the league this week against the luckiest win. Mike D. against Hearn is the game of the week on points: the two highest-scoring teams in the league, both 2-2, both convinced they deserve better. Brett A. gets Danny, Jeff gets Hess, and Mark brings his 150 to Frum, who will need his whole bench to come along this time.

Trade Desk: running backs remain the currency, and the needy keep piling up. Sam has nobody healthy behind Bijan and Hampton, Baker's backup projects under 2 a game, Danny is down three backs, Jeff just lost Breece Hall, and Hess's depth chart is a rumor. The sellers are obvious: Mike D. has Cam Skattebo and Alvin Kamara, and Jordan has Rhamondre Stevenson and Tyler Allgeier. Skattebo to Sam for Luther Burden III fixes Sam's hole with a receiver he's not using. Frum and Jeff are a perfect match: Frum needs a receiver and has Ollie Gordon II, who just scored 17 on his bench; Jeff needs a back and has Khalil Shakir. Brett A. needs a receiver with DeVonta Smith out and has RJ Harvey and Aaron Jones to offer; Mark has Mike Evans and Tee Higgins sitting idle. Move of the week: Danny cutting the Bengals defense after its zero, picking up the Bears, starting them and getting 9. Anti-move of the week: Jordan picking up Marcus Mariota, starting him over Bo Nix, and getting 5.3 from eleven plays in a game he lost by 26.

Keeper Corner: four weeks in, not one keeper in the league is beating the league-average return of about 9 points per dollar. The best bargains are Mike D.'s Javonte Williams at $10 and Brett A.'s Chris Olave at $11, both over 70 points already, and Jordan's Jaxon Smith-Njigba has already cleared 100 points at $18. The big-ticket guys are a mixed bag: Kenneth Walker at $39 has 104 points and is earning it, Jahmyr Gibbs at $71 has 105 and costs about five times as much per point as Javonte, and James Cook at $49 sits at 63.5. The basement belongs to Hearn's Alec Pierce, $10 for under 10 points and now on IR. Sam has already cut one of his keepers, Jaxson Dart, and Hess kept nobody at all, which is starting to look less like a mistake and more like a philosophy. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
